an10.43:1.1: “Sir, how many roots of dispute are there?”
an10.43:1.2: “Upāli, there are ten roots of disputes.
an10.43:1.4: It’s when a mendicant explains what is not an offense as an offense, and what is an offense as not an offense. They explain a light offense as a heavy offense, and a heavy offense as a light offense. They explain a grave offense as a minor offense, and a minor offense as a grave offense. They explain a curable offense as an incurable offense, and an incurable offense as a curable offense. They explain an offense requiring amends as an offense not requiring amends, and an offense not requiring amends as an offense requiring amends.
an10.43:1.5: These are the ten roots of dispute.”
